newsitem.title: USA: Dendrite shares crumble after warning.
newsitem.headline: Dendrite shares crumble after warning.

text.p: The stock of Dendrite International Inc. tumbled Friday, a day after the maker of sales-force management software warned of fourth-quarter losses and disappointing 1997 results due to contract delays.
The stock plunged $11.25 or more than 57 percent to $8.375 on Nasdaq at mid-afternoon.
Late Thursday Dendrite said it expected to report a fourth-quarter loss because it did not receive "certain new business and business-expansion commitments."
It said the delays would adversely affect the revenue and income of the company throughout 1997.
Analysts had expected the Morristown, N.J.-based company to report a profit of 21 cents a share in the fourth quarter and earn 83 cents a share in 1997, according to First Call.
Dendrite earned $2.1 million, or 19 cents a share, on revenues of almost $16 million in the fourth quarter ended Dec. 31, 1995.
The company also pointed to costs from unexpectedly high research and development spending and the hiring of staff to service the product rollouts delayed by customers.
